title: Play
description: A football play. References a formation by id (the formation file in data/formations/) and adds per-player assignments, motions, reads, success/failure analysis, and tags.

aliases.description: Alternate names this play is known by (different terminology trees).

formation.description: ID of the formation this play uses (matches a file in data/formations/). Player labels in assignments must match labels in the referenced formation.

ball_carrier.description: Label of the player who has the ball at the end of the play (e.g. 'HB' for a run, 'QB' for a designed scramble, the receiver who is the primary read for a pass).

primary_read.description: Label of the primary receiver (pass plays).

checkdown.description: Label of the safety-valve receiver if all reads are covered.

motions.description: Pre-snap (or at-snap) motions. Each motion is tagged mandatory or optional.

assignments.description: Per-player assignment. Should cover all 11 players in the referenced formation.

strengths.description: What this play does well — situations and matchups it's built for.

weaknesses.description: Where this play struggles — defensive reactions or matchups it can't beat.

best_vs_defense.description: Defensive coverages or fronts this play attacks well (e.g. 'cover-2', 'over-front', 'cover-3').

common_uses.description: Game situations where you'd typically call this play.

era.description: Era when this play was/is most associated with (e.g. '1990s NFL', 'modern Air Raid').

famous_examples.description: Coaches, teams, or notable instances of this play.

tags.description: Free-form tags. Conventionally includes a level tag (high-school, college, nfl, any-level), philosophy/concept tags (power-run, air-raid, west-coast, spread, gap-scheme), and situation tags (red-zone, short-yardage, hurry-up).

player.description: Player label from the referenced formation (e.g. 'Z', 'HB', 'SLOT').

type.description: Mandatory: the play assumes the motion happened — running it without motion changes the concept. Optional: motion is a check the QB / coach can call (e.g. for matchup leverage), but the play works without it.

end_position.description: Where the motioning player ends up at snap (universal coords). Optional — start position comes from the formation.

snap_on_motion.description: True if the ball is snapped while the player is still in motion (e.g. jet motion). False / omitted means the player is set before snap.

role.description: What the player does on this play. 'handoff' is for the QB on a designed run.

depth_yd.description: Route break depth in yards (for routes), or push depth for blockers.

blocking_scheme.description: Blocking scheme when role is a block variant (e.g. 'down-block', 'kickout', 'pull-around', 'reach', 'man-protection', 'invite-rusher').

is_primary.description: True if this player is the primary read (for routes) or the primary ball-carrier.
